purpose: This tool lets you move a triangle by slides, flips, turns and stretches, and checks what stays the same. You learn which moves keep the shape exactly (rigid) and why two shapes are called congruent.

stops.title: Preimage and image
stops.text: The faint triangle ABC is where you start. The solid blue triangle A'B'C' is the result of your moves. Nothing on the grid is dragged. You choose a move in the panel and press Apply move. A dashed violet line shows the mirror for a flip.
stops.try: Press Apply move once and watch the blue triangle glide into place.

stops.title: Choose a move
stops.text: Slide moves every point the same way. Flip mirrors over a line. Turn spins around a center. Dilate stretches from a center. The sliders below change to match your choice.
stops.try: Open the menu and pick Turn. Notice the new controls.

stops.title: Slide amounts
stops.text: Slide only. These set how far right and how far up. Negative numbers go left or down. The readout lists the rule in coordinates, such as (x + 3, y - 2).
stops.try: Set 3 right and 2 down, press Apply move, and read each corner.

stops.title: Mirror line
stops.text: Flip only. Choose the line to mirror over. Each corner jumps to the other side, the same distance from the line. The readout shows that the order A, B, C turns from counterclockwise to clockwise.
stops.try: Try y = x and see where corner A lands.

stops.title: Dilation factor
stops.text: Dilate only. A factor of 2 doubles every side, and 1 changes nothing. The readout says Not rigid when the sizes change. Center x and center y set the point the shape stretches or turns from. They also work for Turn.
stops.try: Dilate by 2, then read the side lengths in the readout.

stops.title: Apply, Undo, Reset
stops.text: Apply move adds your move to the figure you see now, up to three in a row. Undo takes back the last one. Reset clears all. The readout compares lengths, angles and direction before and after each move.
stops.try: Stack a flip and a slide, then Undo one.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 shows a slide. Step 2 shows a flip. Step 3 shows a dilation that is not rigid. Step 4 asks if the order of two moves matters, using a prediction and your own tests.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: Three questions at the end. A wrong answer explains why.

teacher: Project step 4 and ask for a prediction first: does flip then slide land in the same place as slide then flip? Have students test both orders. Typical misconception: dilation counts as a rigid motion because the shape looks the same. Ask which numbers in the readout changed.
